messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: High error rate detected for tenant PeregrineHealth (tenant_id=ph-0321) in VPC 'us-west-2-vpc-07'. Metric: prefix_kv_hit_rate fell from ~94% to 2.8% over 3m. Latency spikes + request queueing observed. Paging on-call.

sara (SRE): acked, oncall here. Pulling up metrics and recent deploys.

oncall-ops: Paging runtime oncall @matt and eng-ml @devon. Assigning incident lead: sara.

matt (runtime): I'm here, looking at pool dedicated-peregrine-usw2-1. Seeing huge cold-miss rate on prefix cache, KV eviction rate abnormal. Nodes showing elevated GPU time per request.

sara (SRE): timeline: started ~12:10 UTC. Any recent model or config rollouts for that pool?

matt (runtime): No model rollouts in last 24h. There was an autoscale and a large burst of short requests from tenant around 12:05. Suspect prefix explosion/poisoning.

leila (acct): Customer reports latency impacting inference for call center flows. They're seeing 5-10s responses. They will prepare an incident banner if we need them to pause traffic.

devon (eng-ml): Can we quickly check prefix fingerprint distribution for tenant? I can run a top-k prefixes query against telemetry.

matt (runtime): running query now, returning top prefixes and their counts.

incident-bot: System note: autoscaler triggered scale-out at 12:06:42 UTC for pool dedicated-peregrine-usw2-1 (+3 nodes).

matt (runtime): Output: top prefixes: pfx-0001..pfx-0200 normal. But there's a long tail: ~84k unique prefixes in last 10m for tenant ph-0321. Traffic pattern looks like a template leak or client-side per-request nonce in prompt prefix. That will trash prefix KV.

sara (SRE): OK that aligns with cache pollution. Immediate mitigation options: (1) throttle tenant traffic at ingress (2) disable per-tenant prefix caching for this tenant (3) route traffic to fallback model variant (smaller, cheaper) until cleaned. Thoughts?

matt (runtime): I can flip tenant-level prefix_cache_enabled=false for ph-0321 via runtime API. That should stop eviction churn and restore hit-rate for other tenants. Command ready:

```
# curl to flip tenant cache flag
curl -X POST https://internal-api.redwood/runtime/tenants/ph-0321/cache -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" -d '{"prefix_cache_enabled":false}'
```

matt (runtime): Note: flipping will increase token cost per request (no prefix reuse) but reduces latency noise across pool.

leila (acct): Customer OK with temporary increased cost if it stabilizes latency. They asked to notify them before we make changes.

sara (SRE): We'll notify now, and perform action after confirmation. Leila, can you ping customer to confirm immediate temporary disable?

leila (acct): pinged Peregrine on their escalation channel, they gave go-ahead. "Please do whatever reduces latency, we'll accept the extra cost temporarily."

matt (runtime): executing cache flip now. Expect effect within ~30s per node as config propagates.

incident-bot: Action logged: tenant cache flag change requested by matt at 12:22:04 UTC.

matt (runtime): Done. Response: 200 OK. Propagation started.

sara (SRE): Observing metrics... 

(45s pass)

matt (runtime): preliminary: prefix_kv_hit_rate for tenant still low (as expected), but eviction churn dropped by 92%. Aggregate pool hit-rate for shared prefixes rising. Latency tail decreasing.

devon (eng-ml): Good. Once traffic pattern settles, we should re-evaluate whether to enable an LRU cap or more aggressive prefix normalization client-side with Peregrine.

sara (SRE): Customer update drafted: "We've disabled prefix-level caching for your tenant to stop cache pollution causing latency. Our teams are monitoring; we'll follow up with a post-incident analysis and recommended client fixes." Leila will send.

leila (acct): Sent. Customer thanks the team, says call center volume remains high but latency improved on a few checks.

matt (runtime): Running additional mitigation: increase per-tenant QPS limits to protect pool? Actually we should decrease for this tenant until they remediate. Setting soft throttle to 50% of baseline.

```
# set soft throttle
curl -X POST https://internal-api.redwood/quotas/tenants/ph-0321 -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" -d '{"soft_qps":50}'
```

incident-bot: Quota change recorded.

sara (SRE): Marking customer-impacting = yes, Sev=2 (customer latency for enterprise tenant). Notifying oncall rotation for follow-up.

matt (runtime): After cache flip + throttle, pool-level 95th latency dropped from 1.8s -> 320ms over 10m. GPU utilization normalized.

devon (eng-ml): Suggest we capture a sample of offending prefixes and feed to customer devs for quick client patch: likely they are stamping a UUID into prompt prefix.

sara (SRE): I'll collect top-500 pollution prefixes and attach to PM. Running export now.

matt (runtime): Also scheduled rolling restart of 2 nodes that show highest eviction counters to fully clear in-memory KV. Doing sequential restarts to keep capacity.

incident-bot: Maintenance note: rolling restart kicked for node node-asc-12 at 12:35:20 UTC.

(rolling restart 12:35-12:48)

matt (runtime): restarts complete. Post-restart metrics: tenant_kv_hitrate still low for ph-0321 (expected), but overall pool prefix hit-rate back to 88%. Errors for customer reduced to baseline.

sara (SRE): Customer confirmed improved experience. Logs show error rate back to normal. Moving incident to mitigated.

leila (acct): Customer requests a follow-up call to discuss client-side fix and cost impact. Booking for tomorrow 14:00 UTC.

devon (eng-ml): Actions to track: 1) postmortem with root cause (client-prefix-entropy) 2) recommend client change to canonicalize prompts and remove per-request nonces 3) consider server-side prefix normalization heuristics and an LRU cap for tenant prefix sets 4) run traffic replays to verify.

sara (SRE): I'll take postmortem owner. Preliminary severity: Sev2. ETA for write-up 48h. We'll include playbook steps for disabling cache + throttle.

matt (runtime): Follow-up: schedule a config change to enable an automatic detection rule to mark tenant prefix sets with >10k unique prefixes in 10m as "cache-limited" to avoid manual flips.

incident-bot: Incident state: MITIGATED at 12:49:03 UTC by sara.

sara (SRE): Handoff to next oncall @matt for monitoring. Summary for handoff: why (client emitted high-entropy prefixes), what we did (disabled tenant prefix cache, soft-throttle, rolling restarts), impact (latency and error spike for Peregrine; customer-facing improvement after mitigations), follow-ups (postmortem, client fix, detection rule).

matt (runtime): taking it. Will keep 1h watch and will escalate if any regressions.

leila (acct): Thanks all. I'll sync with customer and share postmortem invite.

devon (eng-ml): Adding a note to PR: consider sampling prefix fingerprints into evals to detect client regressions earlier.

sara (SRE): Closing thread, will attach artifacts to the incident ticket. Good work everyone. :tada:
